title: Function: Domain and Range
notes: **Function: Domain and Range:** This topic covers the fundamental concepts of function: domain and range in the mathematics curriculum.
Understanding function: domain and range is essential for solving problems and building higher-level mathematical skills.
Key definitions and theorems related to function: domain and range should be memorized and practiced regularly.
confusion: The domain is about INPUTS (x-values), the range is about OUTPUTS (y-values). Don't mix them up.
f(x) does NOT mean f times x. It means "the value of function f at input x".
For inverse functions: swap x and y, then solve for y. The domain of f becomes the range of f⁻¹ and vice versa.
practice: Find the domain and range of f(x) = √(4-x²).
If f(x) = 2x+3 and g(x) = x², find (f∘g)(x) and (g∘f)(x). Are they equal?
Find the inverse of f(x) = (2x+1)/(x-3) and state its domain.
Determine whether f(x) = x³ is one-to-one and onto from ℝ to ℝ.
universalFacts: The concept of a function is one of the most fundamental ideas in all of mathematics.
Functions model real-world relationships: distance vs time, cost vs quantity, temperature vs altitude.
The vertical line test determines whether a graph represents a function: if any vertical line crosses the graph more than once, it's not a function.
